title: How much does a website cost in Delhi in 2026?
author: ER Freelancer
excerpt: Typical 2026 price ranges for business websites, online stores and web apps in Delhi NCR, what actually changes the quote, and the running costs most people forget.
content:
Ask five developers in Delhi what a website costs and you will hear five very different numbers. The gap is rarely about the developer's rate alone. It comes from what is being built, how much of it is custom, and what the site has to connect to. This guide explains the ranges you will see in 2026, what moves a quote up or down, and how to brief a project so the quotes you receive can actually be compared.

## Typical price ranges in 2026

The figures below come from Hostinger India's 2026 website-cost guide. They are market ranges before GST, not ER Freelancer prices. Use them to sense-check quotes, not as fixed packages.

- **Small static site (1–5 pages), freelancer-built:** ₹10,000 – ₹40,000
- **Dynamic business site with a CMS, freelancer-built:** ₹40,000 – ₹1,50,000
- **Small business site, agency-built:** ₹50,000 – ₹1,50,000
- **WooCommerce store, freelancer-built:** ₹25,000 – ₹1,00,000
- **E-commerce site, agency-built:** ₹1,50,000 – ₹4,00,000 and more
- **Custom web application or start-up platform:** ₹2,50,000 – ₹10,00,000 and more

Source: [Hostinger India — How much does a website cost in India in 2026?](https://www.hostinger.com/in/tutorials/website-cost)

## What actually changes the quote

- **Number of unique page templates.** Ten pages built from two templates cost far less than ten pages that are each designed separately.
- **Custom design versus a theme.** A tailored design system takes longer than adapting a well-built theme, but it is easier to extend later.
- **CMS and editing needs.** If your team will update services, prices or blog posts themselves, the content model and editor training are part of the scope.
- **Integrations.** CRM, WhatsApp, payment gateways, booking systems, ERP or accounting software each add design, development and testing time.
- **Content readiness.** Projects move faster and cost less when text, photos and product data are ready before development starts.
- **Speed and SEO baseline.** Mobile performance, structured data and clean URLs should be in the scope from day one, not bolted on after launch.

## Requirements specific to Indian businesses

- **Payments:** customers expect UPI, plus gateways such as Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree, PhonePe PG or Paytm. Gateways usually charge a per-transaction fee, so compare them before you choose.
- **GST invoices:** paid orders need GST-compliant invoices with GSTIN and HSN/SAC codes.
- **E-commerce rules:** online stores must show seller details and a grievance officer under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.
- **Privacy:** forms that collect personal data should follow the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 — clear, purpose-specific consent that users can withdraw. The DPDP Rules, 2025 are being phased in.

This is practical project guidance, not legal advice.

## Running costs people forget

- **Domain:** about ₹500 – ₹1,500 a year for a .com or .in.
- **Hosting:** about ₹2,000 – ₹8,000 a year for standard or managed WordPress hosting; more for cloud or VPS.
- **Maintenance:** updates, backups and small changes — roughly ₹1,500 – ₹10,000 a year for a small site from a freelancer, more for stores and larger sites.
- **Third-party services:** payment gateway fees, email delivery, paid plugins or apps, and any paid fonts or stock images.

The same Hostinger guide is the source for these ranges.

## How to get quotes you can compare

Send every developer the same short brief:

- What the site must achieve (enquiries, bookings, online sales)
- The pages or page types you need, and who will update them
- Systems it must connect to (WhatsApp, CRM, payment gateway, accounting)
- Whether text, photos and product data are ready
- Your launch window and budget range

Then ask each quote to list deliverables, milestones, what is excluded, who owns the code and accounts, and what support costs after launch. A lower number that excludes hosting, content entry or payment testing is not really cheaper.

## Working with a freelancer in Delhi NCR

If you are in Delhi, Noida or Gurugram, the first discovery meeting can be in person on request, with reviews and handover over video calls and a shared staging link. title: Website checklist for businesses in Dubai and the UAE
author: ER Freelancer
excerpt: Arabic and English layouts, UAE data-protection rules, VAT display, local payment methods and the channels UAE customers use — what to plan before you build.
content:
A website that works well in India, the UK or the US often needs real changes before it works for customers in Dubai and the rest of the UAE. Language direction, data-protection rules, payment methods and the channels people use to contact a business are all different. Use this checklist before you brief a designer or developer.

## 1. Arabic and English, done properly

- Decide early whether the site is English-only, Arabic-only or bilingual. Bilingual sites are common for consumer brands, government-facing businesses and real estate.
- Arabic needs a true right-to-left (RTL) layout — navigation, icons, forms and tables all flip. A mirrored English template rarely looks right.
- Give each language its own URL (for example /en/ and /ar/) and add hreflang tags so search engines show the right version.
- Plan Arabic fonts and line spacing separately; Latin font settings make Arabic text cramped.

## 2. Data protection: PDPL, DIFC and ADGM

- Onshore UAE businesses fall under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection (PDPL).
- Free zones have their own regimes: the DIFC Data Protection Law 2020 and the ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021. Check which one applies to your licence.
- In practice: collect only the data a form needs, explain why, keep a clear privacy notice, and choose hosting and email providers you can document.

Source: [UAE Legislation — Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1972). This is practical project guidance, not legal advice.

## 3. Prices, VAT and invoices

- Prices are usually shown VAT-inclusive; the standard UAE VAT rate is 5%.
- Show the currency clearly (AED) and decide whether you also quote USD for international buyers.
- If you sell online, make sure order confirmations and invoices carry the details your accountant needs.

## 4. Payment methods UAE customers expect

- Card and wallet gateways: Network International (N-Genius), Telr, PayTabs, Checkout.com and Stripe, plus Apple Pay.
- Buy-now-pay-later is popular for retail: Tabby and Tamara.
- If you also sell on marketplaces, plan stock and order sync with Amazon.ae or noon from the start.
- Test the full checkout on mobile, including failed payments and refunds.

## 5. Contact channels

- WhatsApp is the first contact channel for many UAE customers — add a WhatsApp button with a pre-filled message, and route enquiries to someone who answers quickly.
- Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok and Snapchat matter depending on the audience; link the ones you actually keep active.
- Show a local phone number (+971) if you have one, and your working hours in UAE time.

## 6. Industry-specific features

- **Real estate:** property listings with filters, maps, floor plans and enquiry forms that reach the right agent.
- **Tourism and hospitality:** direct booking to reduce OTA commission, multilingual tour pages and WhatsApp confirmations.
- **Logistics:** quote requests and shipment tracking.
- **Retail and D2C:** fast mobile storefronts with local payments and BNPL.

## 7. Working across time zones

The UAE is on UTC+4, and India is 1 hour 30 minutes ahead. That leaves about 8.5 hours of overlap in a normal working day, so an Indian development team can join calls in your morning and early afternoon without late nights on either side.
